title: Materials: float/sink, hard/soft
examples: Teacher, can we test if this leaf will float?
Is wood always hard, or can it be soft too?
How do we know if something will sink before we drop it?

explain.say: Everything is made of a material. Wood, metal, plastic and cloth are materials.
You can feel a material. A rock feels hard. Cotton wool feels soft.
You can put things in water. If it floats, it stays on top. If it sinks, it goes to the bottom.

draw.text: Float stays up. Sink goes down.

explain.say: Before you test, make a guess. Light, flat things often float. Small, heavy things often sink. Then test it to check.

faq.q: How do I know if something is hard or soft?
faq.a: Press it gently with your finger. A hard thing keeps its shape. A soft thing squashes.
asks: What is the difference between hard and soft?
Can I test if something is soft?

faq.q: If something floats, does it mean it is light?
faq.a: Often, but a big wooden raft is heavy, and it floats too. The best way to know is to test it.
asks: Is floating the same as being light?
Why do some heavy things float?

faq.q: Can I predict if something will sink?
faq.a: Yes, you can make a guess. Small things that are heavy for their size often sink. Then test it to check.
asks: How can I guess if something sinks?

faq.a: Most wood is hard, like oak. Some wood, like balsa wood, is soft enough to dent with a fingernail.

faq.q: What is the best way to test if something sinks?
faq.a: Put it gently into a bowl of water. Watch if it stays on top or goes to the bottom.
asks: Should I use water to test?

facts: Rocks are usually described as hard materials.
Cotton wool is an example of a soft material.
Objects that float stay on the surface of the water.
Predicting means guessing what will happen next.

quiz.say: Think about pressing each one. Tap the soft one.
quiz.why: A teddy is soft. It squashes when you press it.

wrong.0: A rock is hard, so it keeps its shape when you press it.
wrong.1: Wood is hard, so it stays the same when you press it.

quiz.say: Watch the stone drop to the bottom. Tap the word for this.
quiz.why: Sinks means it goes down to the bottom of the water.

wrong.1: Floats means it stays on top of the water.
wrong.2: Melts means it turns to liquid, like ice in the sun.

quiz.say: Look at the bowl of water. Tap the thing that floats.
quiz.why: A leaf is light and flat. It stays on top of the water.

wrong.0: A metal key is heavy for its size, so it sinks.
wrong.2: A stone is heavy for its size, so it sinks.
